 veḷiyīṭu
iṉiyamutu patippakam
pi.11 kulmokar kuṭiyiruppu, 
35 cevāliya civāci kaṇēcaṉ cālai, 
tiyākarāyar nakar, ceṉṉai - 600 017. 
to.pē. 2433 9030
patippurai
oḷavai cu.turaicāmip piḷḷai
tamatu ōyvaṟiyā uḻaippāl  tamiḻ āyvuk kaḷattil uyarntu niṉṟavar. 20 ām nūṟṟāṇṭil tamiḻ maṟumalarccikku puttuyir ūṭṭiya tamiḻc cāṉṟōrkaḷuḷ muṉ varicaiyil niṟpavar. naṟṟiṇai, puṟanāṉūṟu, aiṅkuṟunūṟu, patiṟṟuppattu ākiya caṅka nūṟ celvaṅkaḷukku uraivaḷam kaṇṭavar. caiva peruṅkaṭalil mūḻkit tiḷaittavar. uraivēntar eṉṟu tamiḻulakam pōṟṟip pukaḻappaṭṭa oḷavai cu.turaicāmip piḷḷai 1903il piṟantu 1981il maṟaintār. 
 vāḻnta āṇṭukaḷ 78. eḻutiya nūlkaḷ 38. itaṉai  poruḷ vaḻip pirittu “uraivēntar tamiḻttokai” eṉum talaippil 28 tokutikaḷāka veḷi yiṭṭuḷḷōm.
illaṟa ēntalākavum, urainayam kaṇṭa uravōrākavum , naṟṟamiḻ nāvalarākavum, caiva cittāntac cemmalākavum , niṟaipukaḻ eytiya uraivēntarāka vum, pulamaiyilum perum pulamaipeṟṟavarākavum tikaḻntu viḷaṅkiya ipperuntamiḻācāṉiṉ nūlkaḷ aṉaittaiyum oru cēra veḷiyiṭuvatil perumai koḷkiṟōm. ivaruṭaiya nūlkaḷil  em kaikkuk kiṭaikkap peṟāta nūlkaḷ 5. maṟṟum ivar eḻutiya tiruvaruṭpā  nūlkaḷum it tokutikaḷil iṭam peṟavillai. 
  “ palvēṟu kālat tamiḻ ilakkiyaṅkaḷ, uraikaḷ, varalāṟu, kalveṭṭu, camayaṅkaḷ eṉṟiṉṉa tuṟaip palavaṟṟil niṟaipulamai peṟṟavar oḷavai cu .turaicāmi avarkaḷ” eṉṟu mūtaṟiñar va.cupa. māṇikkam avarkaḷālum,
  “iravupakal tāṉaṟiyāṉ iṉtamiḻai vaittu
	 varavu celavaṟiyāṉ vāḻvil - uramuṭaiyāṉ
	 taṉkaṭaṉ tāynāṭṭu makkaṭ kuḻaippatilē
	 muṉkaṭaṉ eṉṟuraikkum ēṟu” 
eṉṟu pāvēntar pāratitācaṉ avarkaḷālum pōṟṟip pukaḻap paṭṭa ip peruntakaiyiṉ nūlkaḷai aṇikalaṉkaḷākak kōrttu, muttumālaiyākak  koṭuttuḷḷōm.   
 avar kālattil vāḻnta camakāla aṟiñarkaḷāl pōṟṟip pukaḻap paṭṭavar.  caiva ulakil taṉakkeṉat taṉiyiṭattaip peṟṟavar.  ivar eḻutiya aṉaittu nūlkaḷ maṟṟum malarkaḷ, itaḻkaḷil veḷivanta kaṭṭuraikaḷaiyellām tēṭit tēṭi eṭuttu orē vīccil veḷiyiṭukiṟōm. 
ittokutikaḷ aṉaittum mikacciṟappāka veḷivaruvataṟku muḻuottuḻaippum utaviyum nalkiyavarkaḷ avaruṭaiya tirumakaṉ oḷavai tu.naṭarācaṉ, marukar irā.kumaravēlaṉ, makaḷ vayiṟṟup peyartti tirumati vēṉilā sṭāliṉ ākiyōr āvar. ivarkaḷ it tamiḻttokaikku takka matippuraiyum aḷittu eṅkaḷukkup perumaic cērttu uḷḷaṉar. ivarkaḷukku neñcam niṟainta naṉṟi
taṉ matippu iyakkattil pērīṭupāṭu koṇṭu  uḻaitta ivvaruntamiḻaṟiñar tamiḻp pakaivarait tam pakaivarākak koṇṭa uyar maṉattiṉarāka vāḻntavar eṉpatai niṉaivil koṇṭu it tokai  nūlkaḷai  ipperuntamiḻ aṟiñariṉ 
107  ām āṇṭu niṉaivāka ulakat tamiḻarkaḷukkup payaṉpaṭum vakaiyil  veḷiyiṭuvatil perumakiḻvu koḷkiṟōm. tamiḻ nūl patippil eṅkaḷiṉ inta ariya muyaṟcikkut tōḷ tantu utavuṅkaḷ.
naṉṟi
- patippāḷar

pērurai varainta peruntamiḻk kaṭal!
poṟputaiyal - maṇikkuviyal
“	nūlukku nūlarumai kāṭṭuvatil nuṇṇaṟiñaṉ
mēlukkuc collavillai vērppalāt - tōlukkuḷ
uḷḷa cuḷaikoṭukkum uṇmai uḻaippāḷaṉ
aḷḷak kuṟaiyāta āṟu”
eṉṟu pāvēntarum,
“payaṉuḷḷa varalāṟṟaittanta tālē
	paraṇartāṉ, paraṇartāṉ tāṅkaḷ! vākku
nayaṅkāṭṭic cevikkuttēṉ tanta tālē
	nakkīrartāṉ tāṅkaḷ inta nāḷil
kayaṉmaṉṉar toḻutamoḻi kāttataṉāl - tol
	kāppiyartāṉ! kāppiyartāṉ tāṅkaḷ! eṅkum
tayaṅkāmal ceṉṟutamiḻ vaḷartta tālē
	tāṅkaḷav-oḷavaitāṉ! oḷavai yētāṉ!”
eṉṟu pukaḻntatōṭu,
	“atiyaṉtāṉ iṉṟillai irunti runtāl
	aṭaṭāvō īteṉṉa vintai! iṅkē
  putiyatāyōr āṇoḷavai eṉavi yappāṉ”
eṉak kaṇṇīr malkak kallaṟai muṉ kaviyaracar mīrā urukiyataiyum nāṭu naṉkaṟiyum.
palvēṟu kālat tamiḻilakkiyaṅkaḷ, uraikaḷ, varalāṟu, kalveṭṭu, camayaṅkaḷ eṉṟiṉṉa tuṟai palavaṟṟil niṟaipulamaiyum ceṟinta cintaṉai vaḷamum peṟṟavar uraivēntar oḷavai turaicāmi avarkaḷ. tūyacaṅkat tamiḻ naṭaiyai eḻuttu
vaṉmaiyilum colvaṉmaiyilum oruṅku pēṇiya taṉit tamiḻppaṇpu oḷavaiyiṉ aṟivāṇmaikkuk kaṭṭiyaṅ kūṟum. eṭṭut tokaiyuḷ aiṅkuṟunūṟu, naṟṟiṇai, puṟanāṉūṟu, patiṟṟuppattu eṉṟa nāṉku tokai nūlkaṭkum uraiviḷakkam ceytār. ivvurai viḷakkaṅkaḷil varalāṟṟuk kuṟippum kalveṭṭuk kuṟippum maṇṭik kiṭakkiṉṟaṉa. aiṅkuṟu nūṟṟuc ceyyuṭkaḷai innūṟṟāṇṭiṉ maraviyal vilaṅkiyal aṟivu taḻuvi nuṭpamāka viḷakkiya uraittiṟaṉ pakkantōṟum paḷicciṭak kāṇalām. urai eḻutuvataṟku muṉ, ēṭukaḷ tēṭi mūlapāṭam tērntu terintu varampu ceytukōṭal ivartam uraiyoḻuṅkākum. tamiḻ ilakkiya varalāṟṟil nāṉku caṅkat tokai nūlkaṭku uraikaṇṭavar eṉṟa taṉipperumaiyar mūtaṟiñar oḷavai turaicāmi āvār. itaṉāl uraivēntar eṉṉum ciṟappup peyarai maturai tiruvaḷḷuvar kaḻakam vaḻaṅkiṟṟu. paranta camayavaṟivum nuṇṇiya caiva cittāntat teḷivum uṭaiyavarātaliṉ civañāṉapōtattukkum ñāṉāmirtattukkum maṇimēkalaiyiṉ camaya kātaikaṭkum ariya uraippaṇi ceytār. cittānta caivattai uraiyālum kaṭṭuraiyālum kaṭṭamainta poḻivukaḷālum parappiya arumai nōkki ‘cittānta kalāniti’ eṉṟa camayappaṭṭattai aṟiñar vaḻaṅkiṉar. cilappatikāram, maṇimēkalai, cīvakacintāmaṇi, cūḷāmaṇi, yacōtara kāviyam eṉṉum aintu kāppiyaṅkaḷiṉ ilakkiya muttukkaḷai oḷivīcac ceytavar. maturaik kumaraṉār, cēramaṉṉar varalāṟu, varalāṟṟukkāṭcikaḷ, nantāviḷakku, oḷavait tamiḻ eṉṟiṉṉa urainaṭai nūlkaḷum tokuttaṟkuriya taṉikkaṭṭuraikaḷum ivartam palpulamaiyaip paṟaicāṟṟuvaṉa.
uraivēntar urai varaiyum muṟai ōru taṉicciṟappu vāyntatu. poruḷ kūṟumpōtu āciriyar varalāṟṟaiyum, avar pāṭutaṟku amainta cūḻnilaiyaiyum, appāṭṭiṉ vāyilāka avar uraikkak karutum uṭkōḷaiyum ovvoru pāṭṭiṉ uraiyilum muṉkūṭṭi eṭutturaikkiṉṟār.
pāṇṭiyaṉ aṟivuṭainampiyiṉ pāṭṭukku urai kūṟuṅkāl, avaṉ varalāṟṟaiyum, avaṉatu pāṭṭiṉ cūḻnilaiyaiyum viriyak kūṟi, muṭivil, “ikkūṟṟu aṟakkaḻivuṭaiyatāyiṉum poruṭpayaṉpaṭa varum ciṟappuṭaittātalaik kaṇṭa pāṇṭiyaṉ aṟivuṭai nampi, taṉ iyalpukku ottiyalvatu tērntu, ataṉai ippāṭṭiṭaip peytu kūṟukiṉṟāṉ eṉṟu muṉmoḻintu, piṉpu pāṭṭait tarukiṉṟār. piṟitōriṭattē kapilar pāṭṭukkup poruḷāṉa nikaḻcciyai viḷakkik kāṭṭi, “neñcukkut tāṉ aṭimaiyākātu taṉakku aḵtu aṭimaiyāyt taṉ āṇaikku aṭaṅki naṭakkumāṟu ceyyum talaivaṉiṭattē viḷaṅkum perumaiyum uraṉum kaṇṭa kapilar ippāṭṭiṉkaṇ uḷḷuṟuttup pāṭukiṉṟār” eṉṟu iyampukiṉṟār. ivvāṟu pāṭṭiṉ muṉṉurai amaivatāl, paṭippōr uḷḷattil appāṭṭaip paṭittu makiḻa vēṇṭum eṉṟa avā eḻuntu tūṇṭu kiṟatu.pāṭṭukkaḷam iṉitu paṭippataṟkēṟṟa uriya iṭattil coṟkaḷaip pirittu ac ciṭṭiruppatu ikkālattu otta muṟaiyākum. ataṉāl iraṇṭāyiram āṇṭukaṭku muṉ tōṉṟiya naṟṟiṇaiyiṉ arumaippāṭu ōraḷavu eḷimai eytukiṟatu.
karumpaik kaṇukkaṇuvākat taṟittuc cuvaikāṇpatu pōlap pāṭṭait toṭartoṭarākap pirittup poruḷ uraippatu paḻaiya uraikārarkaḷāṉa parimēlaḻakar, nacciṉārkkiṉiyar mutaliyōr kaikkoṇṭa muṟaiyākum. ammuṟaiyilēyē ivvuraikaḷ amaintiruppatāl, paṭikkumpōtu pala iṭaṅkaḷ, uraivēntar uraiyō parimēlaḻakar mutaliyōr uraiyō eṉap paṉmuṟaiyum nammai maruṭṭukiṉṟaṉa.
“ilakkaṇanūṟ perumparappum ilakkiyanūṟ
    peruṅkaṭalum ellām āyntu,
kalakkamaṟat tuṟaipōkak kaṟṟuṇarnta
    perumpulamaik kalvi yāḷar!
vilakkakalāt tarukkanūl, meypporuḷnūl,
     vaṭamoḻinūl, mēṟpāl nūlkaḷ
nalakkamikat teḷintuṇarntu nāṭuyya
      naṟṟamiḻ taḻaikka vantār!”
eṉṟu pārāṭṭap peṟum perum pulamaiyāḷarākiya arumpeṟal oḷavaiyiṉ nūlaṭaṅkalai aṅkiṅkellām tēṭiyalaintu tiṭpamum nuṭpamum viḷaṅkap patitta pāṭu naṉiperitākum.
kalaippolivum, karuttutteḷivum, potunōkkum polinta nam uraivēntar, vaḷḷalāriṉ tiruvaruṭpā muḻumaikkum pēruraikaṇṭa peruñcelvam. iḵtu tamiḻp pēḻaikkut tāṅkoṇā aruṭcelvamākum. nūlurai, tiṟaṉurai, poḻivurai eṉṟa muvvarampālum tamiḻk karaiyait tiṇṇitākkiya uraivēntar oḷavai turaicāmi avarkaḷiṉ pukaḻuraiyai niṉaintu avar nūlkaḷai nammutalvar kalaiñar nāṭṭuṭaimai ākkiyataṉ payaṉākat  ipputaiyalait iṉiyamutu patippakam veḷiyiṭukiṉṟatu. iṉiyamutu patippaka urimaiyāḷar, tamiḻmaṇ patippakattiṉ  urimaiyāḷar kō.iḷavaḻakaṉāriṉ aruntavapputalvi i.tamiḻamutu āvār.   
īṭariya tamiḻārvap piḻampākavum, vīṟuṭaiya tamiḻppatippu vēntarākavum viḷaṅkum naṇpar iḷavaḻakaṉ tām peṟṟa peruñcelvam muḻuvataiyum tamiḻiṉat taṇal taṇiyalākāteṉa naṟuneyyūṭṭi vaḷarppavar. tamiḻmaṇ patippakam avartam neñcak kaṉalukku vaḻikōluvatākum. avariṉ celvamakaḷār avar vaḻiyil naṭantu    iṉiyamutu patippakam vaḻi, mutal veḷiyīṭāka eṉtantaiyāriṉ aṉaittu ākkaṅkaḷaiyum (tiruvaruṭpā tavira)  payaṉpeṟum vakaiyil veḷiyiṭukiṟār. ippatippup putaiyalai - poṟkuviyalai  tamiḻulakam iru kaiyēnti varavēṟkum eṉṟē karutukiṟōm.
oḷavai naṭarācaṉ

nuḻaivāyil
cemmoḻit tamiḻiṉ cevviyal ilakkiyap paṉuvalkaḷukku uraivaḻaṅkiya cāṉṟōrkaḷuḷ talaimakaṉāy niṟkum cemmal ‘uraivēntar’ oḷavai cu.turaicāmi piḷḷai avarkaḷāvār. pattuppāṭṭiṟkum, kalittokaikkum cīvakacintāmaṇikkum  nallurai tanta nacciṉārkkiṉiyarukkup piṉ, āṟu nūṟṟāṇṭukaḷ kaḻittu, aiṅkuṟunūṟu, puṟanāṉūṟu, patiṟṟuppattu, naṟṟiṇai, yacōtara kāviyam ākiya nūlkaḷukku uraiyeḻutiya perumai oḷavai avarkaḷaiyē cārum.  caṅka nūlkaḷukkuc cemmaiyāṉa urai tīṭṭiya mutal ‘tamiḻar’ ivar eṉṟu perumitam koḷḷalām.
eḻuttāṟṟalum pēccāṟṟalum mikka oḷavai 1903 ām āṇṭu cepṭampar aintām nāḷ tōṉṟi, 1981ām āṇṭu ēpral mūṉṟām nāḷ pukaḻuṭampu eytiyavar. tamiḻum caivamum tam irukaṇkaḷākak koṇṭu iṟutivarai ceyaṟpaṭṭavar.  cintai civaperumāṉaic cintikka, cennā ainteḻuttu mantirattaic ceppa, tirunīṟu neṟṟiyil tikaḻa, uruttirākkam mārpiṉil uruḷat taṉ muṉṉar irukkum ciṟu cāymēcaiyil tāḷkaḷaik koṇṭu, uruṇṭu tiraṇṭa eḻutukōlait tiṟantu eḻutat toṭaṅkiṉārāṉāl maṇikkaṇakkil uṇṭi mutalāṉavai maṟantu kaṭṭuraikaḷaiyum, kaṉinta uraikaḷaiyum eḻutikkoṇṭē iruppār.  centamiḻ avar eḻutaṭṭum eṉṟu kāttiruppatupōl aruviyeṉak koṭṭum.  niṉaivāṟṟalil vallavarātalāl eḻuntu ceṉṟu vēṟu nūlkaḷaip pakkam puraṭṭi pārkka vēṇṭum eṉṉum nilai avarukkiruntatillai.
ententa nūlkaḷukkuc cemmaiyāṉa uraiyillaiyō avaṟṟiṟkē uraiyeḻutuvatu eṉṉum koḷkai uṭaiyavar avar. ataṉāl atuvarai cīriya urai kāṇappeṟāta aiṅkuṟunūṟu, patiṟṟuppattu ākiyavaṟṟiṟkum, muḻumaiyāṉa uraiyaip peṟṟirāta puṟanāṉūṟṟukkum oḷavai urai varaintār. piṉṉar naṟṟiṇaikkup putturai tēvaippaṭuvatai aṟintu, muṉṉaiya patippukaḷil irunta piḻaikaḷai nīkkip putiya pāṭaṅkaḷait tērntu virivāṉa uraiyiṉai eḻuti iru tokutikaḷāka veḷiyiṭṭār.
cittānta kalāniti eṉṉum perumai peṟṟa oḷavai, civañāṉapōtac ciṟṟurai viḷakkattai eḻutiyatōṭu, ‘irumpukkaṭalai’ eṉak karutappeṟṟa ñāṉāmirta nūlukkum urai tīṭṭiṉār.  caiva mānāṭukaḷukkut talaimai tāṅkic coṟpoḻivukaḷ  nikaḻttiṉār.  tam uraikaḷ palavaṟṟaik kaṭṭuraikaḷ ākkiṉār.  centamiḻc celvi, centamiḻ, kumarakuruparaṉ, cittāntam mutalāṉa pala itaḻkaḷukkuk kaṭṭuraikaḷai vaḻaṅkiṉār.
peruntakaip peṇṭir, maturaik kumaraṉār, oḷavait tamiḻ, paraṇar mutalāṉa kaṭṭurai nūlkaḷai eḻutiṉār. avar ārāyccit tiṟaṉukkuc cāṉṟāka viḷaṅkum nūl ‘paṇṭai nāḷaic cēramaṉṉar varalāṟu’ eṉṉum āyvu nūlākum.  aṇṇāmalaip palkalaik kaḻakattil oḷavai paṇiyāṟṟiyapōtu  ārāynteḻutiya ‘caiva camaya ilakkiya varalāṟu’ attuṟaiyil iṇaiyaṟṟatāka iṉṟum viḷaṅkukiṟatu.
caṅka nūlkaḷukku oḷavai varainta urai kaṟṟōr aṉaivaruṭaiya neñcaiyum kavarntatākum.  ovvoru pāṭṭaiyum alaci ārāyum paṇpuṭaiyavar avar.  muṉṉaiya uraiyāciriyarkaḷ piḻaipaṭṭiruppiṉ tayaṅkātu maṟuppurai taruvar.  takka pāṭa vēṟupāṭukaḷait tērnteṭuttu mūlattaic cemmaippaṭuttu vatil avarukku iṇaiyāṉavar evarumilar.  ‘uḻutacāl vaḻiyē uḻum iḻutai neñciṉar’ allar.  perumpālum paḻamaikku amaiti kāṇpār.  atē nērattil putumaikkum vaḻi ceyvār.
tamiḻōṭu āṅkilam, vaṭamoḻi, pāli mutalāṉavaṟṟaik kaṟṟut tērntavar avar.  maṇimēkalaiyiṉ iṟutip pakutikku uraiyeḻutiya nilai vantapōtu avar muṉaintu pālimoḻiyaik kaṟṟuṇarntu ataṉ piṉṉarē anta uraiyiṉaic ceytār eṉṟāl avaratu īṭupāṭṭuṇarvai naṉku uṇaralām.  eppōtum ētēṉum āṅkila nūlaip paṭikkum iyalpuṭaiyavar oḷavai avarkaḷ.  tirukkuṟaḷ paṟṟiya oḷavaiyiṉ āṅkilac coṟpoḻivu nūlāka accil vantapōtu palarāl pārāṭṭap peṟṟamai avartam āṅkilap pulamaikkuc cāṉṟu pakarvatākum.  camaya nūlkaḷukku uraiyeḻutuṅkāl vaṭamoḻi nūlkaḷiliruntu mēṟkōḷ kāṭṭuvatum, karuttukaḷai viḷakkuvatum avar iyalpu.  atumaṭṭumaṉṟi, oḷavai avarkaḷ caṭṭanūl nuṇukkaṅkaḷaiyum kaṟṟaṟinta pulamaic celvar.
oḷavai avarkaḷ kaṭṭurai puṉaiyum vaṉmai peṟṟavar.  kalaipayil teḷivu avarpāluṇṭu.  nuṇmāṇ nuḻaipulattōṭu avar tīṭṭiya kaṭṭuraikaḷ eṇṇila. avai caṅka ilakkiyap poruḷ paṟṟiyaṉa āyiṉum, camayac cāṉṟōr paṟṟiyaṉa āyiṉum putiya ceytikaḷ avaṟṟil alaipōl puraṇṭu varum.  oḷavai naṭai taṉinaṭai.  aṟivu nuṭpattaiyum karuttāḻattaiyum antac cemmānta naṭaiyil avar koṇṭuvantu tarumpōtu kaṟpār uḷḷam evvāṟu iruppārō, ataippōṉṟē avar tamiḻ naṭaiyum cintaṉaip pōkkum amaintiruntatu viyappukkuriya oṉṟu.
oḷavai āṟṟiya aruntamiḻp paṇikaḷuḷ talaiyāyatu paḻantamiḻ nūlkaḷukku aṟivārnta uraikaḷai vakuttut tantamaiyē ākum.  etaṉaiyum kāytal uvattaliṉṟi cīrtūkkip pārkkum naṭunilaip pōkku avariṭam ūṉṟiyirunta oru paṇpu.  avar urai ciṟantamaintataṟkāṉa kāraṇam iraṇṭu.  mutalāvatu, vaiṇava uraikaḷil kāṇappeṟṟa ‘patacāram’ kūṟum muṟai.  tām uraiyeḻutiya aṉaittup paṉuvalkaḷilum kāṇappeṟṟa coṟṟoṭarkaḷai intap patacāra muṟaiyilē aṇuki ariya ceytikaḷai aḷittuḷḷār.  iraṇṭāvatu, caṭṭa nuṇukkaṅkaḷait terivikkum nūlkaḷilamainta āyvuraikaḷum tīrppuraikaḷum avartam tamiḻ āyvukkut tuṇai niṉṟa tiṟam.  ‘jūrispurūṭaṉs’ ‘lā āḵp ṭārṭs’ mutalāṉavai paṟṟiya āṅkila nūlkaḷait tām paṭittatōṭu eṉṉaip pōṉṟavarkaḷaiyum paṭikka vaittār.  vaṭamoḻit tarukkamum vēṟupiṟa aḷavai nūlkaḷum palvakaic camaya aṟivum avar uraiyiṉ cemmaikkut tuṇai niṉṟaṉa.  aṉaittiṟkum mēlāka varalāṟṟuṇarvu illāta ilakkiya aṟivu payaṉaṟṟatu, ilakkiyap payiṟci illāta varalāṟṟāyvu vīṇāṉatu eṉṉum karuttuṭaiyavar avar.  ātalāl eṇṇaṟṟa varalāṟṟu nūlkaḷaiyum, āyirakkaṇakkāṉa kalveṭṭukaḷaiyum āḻntu paṭittu, maṉattiliruttit tām ilakkiyattiṟku urai varaintapōtu naṉku payaṉpaṭuttik koṇṭār.  ñāṉacampantap peruntakaiyiṉ tiruvōttūrt tēvārat tiruppatikattiṟku mutaṉmutalāka uraiyeḻutat toṭaṅkiya kālantoṭṭu iṟutiyāka vaṭalūr vaḷḷaliṉ tiruvaruṭpāviṟkup pērurai eḻuti muṭikkum varaiyilum, varalāṟu, kalveṭṭu, tarukkam, ilakkaṇam mutalāṉavaṟṟiṉ aṭippaṭaiyilēyē uraikaḷai eḻutiṉār.  tēvaippaṭumpoḻutu uyiriyal, payiriyal, uḷaviyal tuṟai nūlkaḷiliruntum viḷakkaṅkaḷai aḷikkat tavaṟavillai.  ivaṟṟai avartam aiṅkuṟunūṟṟu virivurai teḷivupaṭuttum.
oḷavai avarkaḷiṉ nuṭpa uraikku oru cāṉṟu kāṭṭalām.  avaruṭaiya naṟṟiṇaip patippu veḷivarumvarai atil kaṭavuḷ vāḻttup pāṭalāka amainta ‘mānilañ cēvaṭi yāka’ eṉṉum pāṭalait tirumāṟku uriyatākavē aṉaivarum karutiṉar.  piṉṉattūrār tam uraiyil avvāṟē eḻuti iruntār.  intap pāṭalai iyaṟṟiyavar pāratam pāṭiya peruntēvaṉār.  ivarē vēṟu cila caṅkattokai nūlkaḷukkum kaṭavuḷ vāḻttu iyaṟṟiyavar.  avaṟṟilellām civaṉaip pāṭiyavar naṟṟiṇaiyil maṭṭum vēṟu iṟaivaṉaip pāṭuvarō eṉṟu cintitta oḷavai, muḻuppāṭalukkum civaneṟiyilēyē uraiyai eḻutiṉār.
oḷavai urai amaikkum pāṅkē taṉittaṉmaiyāṉatu.  mutalil pāṭalaip pāṭiya āciriyar peyar paṟṟiyum avartam ūrpaṟṟiyum viḷakkam taruvar.  tēvaippaṭṭāl kalveṭṭu mutalāṉavaṟṟiṉ tuṇaikoṇṭu peyarkaḷaic cemmaip paṭuttuvar.  tumpi cokiṉaṉār ivar āyvāl ‘tumpaic cokiṉaṉār’ āṉār.  neṭuṅkaḻuttup paraṇar oḷavaiyāl ‘neṭuṅkaḷattup paraṇar’  eṉṟāṉār.  paḻaiya māṟpittiyār oḷavai uraiyil ‘mārip pittiyār’ āka māṟiṉār.  veṟipāṭiya kāmakkaṇṇiyār oḷavaiyiṉ karampaṭṭut tūymaiyāki ‘veṟipāṭiya kāmakkāṇiyār’ āṉār.  ivvāṟu ettaṉaiyō caṅkap peyarkaḷ ivarāl cemmai aṭaintuḷḷaṉa.
aṭutta nilaiyil, pāṭaṟ piṉṉaṇic cūḻalai nayampaṭa uraiyāṭaṟ pōkkil eḻutuvar.  ataṉ piṉ pāṭal  muḻutum cīrpirittut tarappaṭum. aṭuttu, pāṭal toṭarkaḷukkup patavuraip pōkkil viḷakkam amaiyum.  piṉṉar ētukkaḷālum eṭuttukkāṭṭukaḷālum coṟṟoṭarp poruḷkaḷai viḷakki eḻutuvar.  tēvaippaṭum iṭaṅkaḷil takka ilakkaṇak kuṟippu kaḷaiyum mēṟkōḷkaḷaiyum tavaṟātu vaḻaṅkuvar.  uḷḷuṟaip poruḷ ētēṉum pāṭalil irukkumāṉāl avaṟṟait teḷivu paṭuttuvar. muṉpiṉ varum pāṭal toṭarkaḷai naṉkāyntu ‘viṉaimuṭipu’ taruvatu avar vaḻakkam.  iṟutiyākap pāṭaliṉkaṇ amainta meyppāṭu īteṉṟum, payaṉ īteṉṟum teḷivu paṭuttuvar.
oḷavaiyiṉ urainuṭpattiṟku oru cāṉṟu.  ‘pakaivar pul ārka’ eṉpatu aiṅkuṟunūṟṟu nāṉkām pāṭalil varum oru toṭar.  maṉitar pul ārtal uṇṭō eṉṉum viṉā eḻukiṟatu.  eṉavē, uraiyil ‘pakaivar tam perumitam iḻantu pullaricic cōṟuṇka’ eṉa viḷakkam taruvar.  ikkaruttē koṇṭu, cēṉāvaraiyarum ‘puṟṟiṉṟal uyartiṇaikku iyaipiṉṟu eṉappaṭātu’ eṉṟār eṉa mēṟkōḷ kāṭṭuvar.  maṟṟoru pāṭṭil ‘mutalaip pōttu muḻumīṉ ārum’ eṉa varukiṟatu. itil muḻumīṉ eṉpataṟku ‘muḻu mīṉaiyum’ eṉṟu poruḷ eḻutātu, ‘iṉi vaḷarcci yillaiyāmāṟu muṟṟa mutirnta mīṉ” eṉṟu uraiyeḻutiya tiṟam aṟiyattakkatu.
oḷavai iḷampūraṇar, nacciṉārkkiṉiyar mutalāṉa paḻaiya uraiyāciriyarkaḷaiyum maṟukkum āṟṟal uṭaiyavar.  cāṉṟāka, ‘maṉainaṭu vayalai’ (aiṅ.11) eṉṉum pāṭalai iḷampūraṇar ‘kiḻavaṉai makaṭūup pulampu peritākaliṉ, alamaruḷ perukiya kāmattu mikutiyum’ eṉpataṟku eṭuttukkāṭṭuvar.  āṉāl, oḷavai atai maṟuttu, “maṟṟu, ippāṭṭu, alamaruḷ  perukiya kāmattu mikutikkaṇ nikaḻum kūṟṟākātu talaimakaṉ koṭumaikku amaiti yuṇarntu orumaruṅku amaitalum, avaṉ pirivāṟṟāmaiyait tōḷmēl ēṟṟi amaiyāmaikku ētu kāṭṭutalum cuṭṭi niṟṟaliṉ, avar kūṟuvatu poruntāmai yaṟika” eṉṟu iṉimaiyāka eṭutturaippar.
“taṉ pārpput tiṉṉum aṉpil mutalai” eṉṉum pāṭal talaivaṉaiyum vāyilkaḷaiyum ikaḻntu talaivi kūṟuvatākum.  āṉāl, itaṉaip pērāciriyarum, nacciṉārkkiṉiyarum tattam tolkāppiya uraikaḷil tōḻi kūṟṟu eṉṟu terivittuḷḷaṉar.  oḷavai ivaṟṟai nayampaṭa maṟuttu viḷakkam kūṟit ‘tōḻi kūṟṟeṉṟal nirampāmai aṟika’ eṉṟu teḷivuṟuttuvar.  ivvāṟu iḷampūraṇar, pērāciriyar, nacciṉārkkiṉiyar uḷḷiṭṭa aṉaivaraiyum takka cāṉṟukaḷōṭu maṟutturaikkum tiṟam karutiyum uraiviḷakkac cemmai karutiyum ikkālac cāṉṟōr aṉaivarum oḷavaiyai ‘uraivēntar’ eṉap pōṟṟiṉar.
oḷavai ovvoru nūlukkum eḻutiya uraikaḷiṉ māṇpukaḷai eṭutturaippiṉ perunūlāka viriyum.  tokuttuk kūṟa virumpiṉālō eñci niṟkum.  kaṟpōr tāmē virumpi nukarntu tuyppiṉ urait tiṟaṉkaḷaik kaṇṭuṇarntu viyantu niṟpar eṉpatu tiṇṇam.
oḷavaiyiṉ aṉaittu urainūlkaḷaiyum, kaṭṭurai nūlkaḷaiyum, ilakkiya varalāṟṟu nūlkaḷaiyum, pēruraikaḷaiyum, kaviṉmiku taṉik kaṭṭuraikaḷaiyum, piṟavaṟṟaiyum pakuttum tokuttum koṇṭuvarutal eṉpatu mērumalaiyaik kaikkuḷ aṭakkum perumpaṇi.  tamiḻīḻam toṭaṅki ayalnāṭukaḷ palavaṟṟilum, tamiḻnāṭṭiṉ mūlai muṭukkukaḷilum āka, eṅkeṅkō citaṟikkiṭanta ariya kaṭṭuraikaḷaiyellām tēṭittiraṭṭit takka vakaiyil patippikkum paṇiyil iṉiyamutu patippakam muyaṉṟu veṟṟi peṟṟuḷḷatu.  oḷavai nūlkaḷait tokuppatōṭu nillāmal muṟṟilum paṭittuṇarntu tuyttu makiḻntu tokuti tokutikaḷākap pakuttu veḷiyiṭum iṉiyamutu patippakam nam aṉaivaruṭaiya matippiṟkum pārāṭṭiṟkum naṉṟikkum uriyatu.  ippatippakattiṉ urimaiyāḷar celvi i.tamiḻamutu tamiḻmaṇ patippakattiṉ urimaiyāḷariṉ makaḷ āvār. vāḻka avartam tamiḻppaṇi.  vaḷarka avartam tamiḻttoṇṭu.  ulakeṅkum malarka tamiḻāṭci. vaḷampeṟuka. ittokuppukaḷ uraivēntar tamiḻttokai eṉum talaippil ‘iṉiyamutu’ patippakattiṉ vaḻiyāka veḷivaruvatai varavēṟṟu tamiḻulakam tāṅkip piṭikkaṭṭum. tūkki niṟuttaṭṭum eṉṟu neñcāra vāḻttukiṟēṉ.
 muṉaivar irā.kumaravēlaṉ

taṇṭamiḻācāṉ uraivēntar
uraivēntar oḷavai. turaicāmi avarkaḷ, poṉṟāp pukaḻuṭaiya paintamiḻc cāṉṟōr āvār. ‘uraivēntar’ eṉavum, caiva cittānta kalāniti eṉavum centamiḻp pulam ivaraic cemmāntu aḻaikkiṟatu. naṉṉeṟip paṭarum toṉṉalap poruḷviḷakkam kāṭṭi nūlukku nūlarumai ceytu eññāṉṟum nilaitta pukaḻ īṭṭiya uraivēntariṉ naṟṟiṟam vāynta coṟṟamiḻ nūlkaḷai vakai tokaippaṭutti veḷiyiṭum tamiḻmaṇ patippakattāriṉ aruntoṇṭu aḷappariyatākum.
oḷavaikkīnta arunellik kaṉiyai aritiṉ muyaṉṟu peṟṟavaṉ atiyamāṉ. atupōl iṉiyamutu patippakam oḷavai turaicāmi avarkaḷiṉ kaṉiyamutu kaṭṭuraikaḷaiyum, ilakkiya nūluraikaḷaiyum, tiṟaṉāyvu uraikaḷaiyum peritum muyaṉṟu kaṇṭaṟintu tokuttu veḷiyiṭṭuḷḷaṉar. ivartam arumperumpaṇi, tamiḻulakam talaimēṟ koḷaṟkuriyatākum.
naṉipulamaicāl cāṉṟōr uṭaiyatu toṇṭai nāṭu; appakutiyil amainta tiṇṭivaṉattiṟku arukil uḷḷa oḷavaiyārkuppattil 1903-ām āṇṭu teḷḷu tamiḻnaṭaikku oru tuḷḷal piṟantatu.  aruḷtiru cuntarampiḷḷai, cantiramati ammaiyār ākiya iṇaiyarukku aintām makaṉāka (iraṭṭaik kuḻantai - uṭaṉ piṟantatu peṇmakavu)p piṟantār. ñāṉap pāluṇṭa campantap perumāṉpōṉṟu iḷamaiyilēyē oḷavai avarkaḷ  āṟṟal niṟaintu viḷaṅkiṉār. tiṇṭivaṉattil tamatu paḷḷippaṭippai muṭittu vēlūril palkalaip paṭippait toṭarntār. āyiṉ iṭainilaip palkalai paṭikkum nilaiyil paṭippait toṭara iyalāmaṟ pōyiṟṟu.
eṉavē, uraivēntar tūymaip paṇiyāḷarākap paṇiyēṟṟār; cila mātaṅkaḷē appoṟuppil iruntavar mīṇṭum tam kalviyait toṭarntār. tamiḻ mītūrnta aḷapparum paṟṟāl karantait tamiḻc caṅkat talaivar tamiḻavēḷ umā makēcuvaram piḷḷai, na.mu.vēṅkaṭacāmi nāṭṭār mutalāṉa tamiḻp pērācāṉkaḷiṭam payiṉṟār; vittuvāṉ paṭṭamum peṟṟār. uraivēntar, centamiḻk kalviyaip pōṉṟē āṅkilap pulamaiyum peṟṟiruntār.
“	kulaṉaruḷ teyvam koḷkaimēṉmai
kalaipayil teḷivu kaṭṭurai vaṉmai
nilamalai niṟaikōl malarnikar māṭciyum
amaipavaṉ nūlurai āciriyaṉ”
eṉum  ilakkaṇam muḻumaiyum amaiyap peṟṟavar uraivēntar.
uyarnilaip paḷḷikaḷ, tiruppati tiruvēṅkaṭavaṉ kīḻtticaik kallūri, citamparam aṇṇāmalai palkalaik kaḻakam, maturai tiyākarāyar kallūri eṉa ivartam āciriyap paṇikkālam amaintatu. āciriyar paṇiyil, taṉ āṟṟalait tiṟampaṭa veḷippaṭuttiṉār. eṉavē, pulavar. kā. kōvintaṉ, vittuvāṉ mā.irākavaṉ mutalāṉa talaimāṇākkarkaḷai uruvākkiṉār. itaṉōṭamaiyātu, eḻuttup paṇiyilum mikunta ārvattōṭum , tamiḻāḻattōṭum uraivēntar īṭupaṭṭār. avar caṅka ilakkiya uraikaḷ, kāppiyac curukkaṅkaḷ, varalāṟṟu nūlkaḷ, caivacittānta nūlkaḷ eṉap paltiṟappaṭṭa nūlkaḷ eḻutiṉār.
tam eḻuttup paṇiyāl, tamiḻ kūṟu nallulakam pōṟṟip pārāṭṭum perumai peṟṟār uraivēntar. oḷavaiyavarkaḷ  tam nūlkaḷ vāyilāka putumaic cintaṉaikaḷai ulakiṟku neṟikāṭṭi uyvittār. poṉṉēpōl pōṟṟaṟkuriya muṉṉōr moḻip poruḷil potintuḷḷa māṉiṭaviyal, aṟiviyal, poruḷiyal, vilaṅkiyal, varalāṟu, araciyal eṉap paṉṉaruñ ceytikaḷai urai kūṟumukattāṉ eḷiyōrum uṇarumpaṭic ceytavar uraivēntar.
eṭuttukkāṭṭāka, camaṇacamayac cāṉṟōrkaḷ coṟ pōril vallavarkaḷ eṉṟum kūṟumiṭattu uraivēntar pala cāṉṟukaḷ kāṭṭi valiyuṟuttukiṟār.
“iṉi, camaṇa camayac cāṉṟōrkaḷaip pārāṭṭum kalveṭṭukkaḷ palavum, avartam coṟpōr vaṉmaiyiṉaiyē peritum eṭuttōtukiṉṟaṉa. ciravaṇapelakōlāvil kāṇappaṭum kalveṭṭukaḷ ellāvaṟṟilum ivarkaḷ piṟa camayattavarōṭu coṟpōr ceytu peṟṟa veṟṟic ciṟappaiyē vitantōtuvataik kāṇkiṉṟōm. piṟa camayattavar palarum caivarum, pācupatarum, puttarum, kāpālikarumākavē kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉar. irāṭṭirakūṭa aracaruḷ oruvaṉeṉṟu karutappaṭum kiruṣṇarāyareṉṉum aracaṉ intirananti eṉṉum cāṉṟōrai nōkki umatu peyar yātu? eṉṟu kēṭka, avar taṉ peyar paravātimallaṉ eṉpatu eṉṟu kūṟiyiruppatu oru nalla cāṉṟākum. tiruñāṉa campantarum avarkaḷaic ‘cāvāyum vātucey cāvār” (147:9) eṉpatu kāṇka. ivaṟṟāl camaṇac cāṉṟōr coṟpōril pērārvamuṭaiyavar eṉpatu peṟappaṭum. paṭavē, tōlā moḻit tēvarum camaṇ cāṉṟōrātalāl coṟpōril mikka ārvam koṇṭiruppār eṉṟeṇṇutaṟku iṭamum, tōlāmoḻit tēvar eṉṉum peyarāl avveṇṇattiṟkup paṟṟukkōṭum peṟukiṉṟōm. innūṟkaṇ, ‘tōlā nāviṉ cuccutaṉ’ (41) ‘kaṟṟavaṉ kaṟṟavaṉ karutum kaṭṭuraikku uṟṟaṉa uṟṟa uytturaikkum āṟṟalāṉ (150) eṉpaṉa mutalāka varuvaṉa akkaruttukku ātaravu tarukiṉṟaṉa. nakaiccuvai paṟṟiyurai nikaḻntapōtum ivvāciriyar coṟpōrē poruḷākak koṇṭu,
“	vātam vellum vakaiyātatu veṉṉil
ōti vella luṟuvārkaḷai eṉkai
kōtukoṇṭa vaṭiviṉ taṭiyālē
mōti velvaṉ urai muṟṟuṟa eṉṟāṉ’
eṉpatum piṟavum ivarkkuc coṟpōrk kaṇ irunta vēṭkai ittaṉmait teṉpatai vaṟpuṟuttukiṉṟaṉa.
cūḷāmaṇic curukkattiṉ muṉṉuraiyil  kāṇappaṭum ippakuti camaya varalāṟṟukku ōr eṭuttukkāṭṭākum. iṅṅaṉam pallāṟṟāṉum palvēṟu ceytikaḷai viḷakkiyuraikkum uraippāṅku āyvāḷarukku arumaruntāy amaikiṟatu. kalveṭṭu āyvum, ōlaiccuvaṭikaḷ caripārttalum, ivaratu aṟivāynta ārāyccip pulamaikkuc cāṉṟu pakarvaṉa.
nīriṉum āraḷaviṉatāyp pulamaiyum, malaiyiṉum māṉap peritāy naṟpaṇpum vāykkap peṟṟavar uraivēntar. ivartam naṉṟi maṟavāp paṇpiṟku ōr eṭuttuk kāṭṭāka oru ceytiyaik kūṟalām. karantait tamiḻc caṅkattil taṉṉaip pōṟṟip puranta tamiḻavēḷ umā makēcuvaram piḷḷaiyiṉ niṉaivu nāḷil uṇṇānōṉpum, mauṉa nōṉpum iruttalai vaḻakkamākak koṇṭiruntār.
“	tāyāki uṇpittāṉ; tantaiyāy    aṟivaḷittāṉ; cāṉṟō ṉāki
āyāta nūlpalavum āyvittāṉ
   avvap pō tayarnta kālai
ōyāmal nalamuraittu ūkkuvittāṉ;
    iṉiyārai yuṟuvēm; antō
tēyāta pukaḻāṉtaṉ ceyal niṉaintu
    uḷam tēyntu citaikiṉṟēmāl”
eṉum varuttam tōynta kaiyaṟu pāṭal pāṭit taṉṉuḷam urukiṉār.
ivartam aruntamiḻp perumakaṉār oḷavai.naṭarācaṉār uraivēntariṉ nūlkaḷai nāṭṭuṭaimaiyākkutalil perumpaṅkāṟṟiyavar. avartam perumuyaṟciyum, iṉiyamutu patippakattāriṉ arumuyaṟciyum iṉṟu tamiḻulakiṟkuk kiṭaitta paricilkaḷām.
uraivēntariṉ nūlkaḷaic ‘camaya ilakkiya uraikaḷ, nūṟ curukkaṅkaḷ, ilakkiya ārāycci, kāviya nūlkaḷ- uraikaḷ, ilakkiya varalāṟu, caiva cittānta nūlkaḷ, varalāṟu, caṅka ilakkiyam, kaṭṭurai āyvukaḷiṉ tokuppu’  eṉappakuttum tokuttum veḷiyiṭum iṉiyamutu patippaka urimaiyāḷar celvi i.tamiḻamutu, tamiḻmaṇ patippaka urimaiyāḷar  tiru. kō.iḷavaḻakaṉār avarkaḷiṉ aruntavap putalvi āvār. avarukkut tamiḻulakam eṉṟum talaimēṟkoḷḷum kaṭappāṭu uṭaiyatākum.
“	paḷḷimutal palkalaic cālaivarai pāṅkeṇṇik
koḷmutal ceyyum koṭaimaḻai veḷḷat tēṉ
pāyāta ūruṇṭō? uṇṭā uraivēntai
vāyāra vāḻttāta vāy”
eṉap pāvēntar koñcu tamiḻp paṉuvalāl neñcu makiḻap pāṭukiṟār. uraivēntar tam eḻuttulakac cātaṉaikaḷaik kālac cuvaṭṭil aḻuttamuṟa veḷiyiṭum iṉiyamutu patippakattārai maṉamāra vāḻttuvōmāka!
vāḻiya  tamiḻ nalam!

INTRODUCTION
Tiru Avvai Duraiswamy Pillai of the Annamalai University is well known as the modern commentator on Sangam works. He now gives the world of Tamil Scholars his commentary on Patirruppattu.
Patirruppattu is the only available source book of ancient Cera history. Among all the Sangam works this is unique in being a Collection of the poems on Ceras. Ten great poets had sung the greatness of ten great Cera kings. Unfortunately of the hundred verses, the first ten and the last ten, probably singing the glories of Utiyan and Yanaikkan Mantaram Ceral Irumporai respectively, are missing. There were two ruling Cera families that of Utian and that of Antuvan, the former being the senior and the main Cera line of Vanchi; the latter being the Irumporai line of Tondi. The second Ten and the third Tens belong to the two sons of Uthiyan viz., Imaya Varamban Netun Ceral Athan and Palyanaic - Celkezhu Kuttuvan. The fourth, the fifith and the sixth Tens relate respectively to the sons of Netun Ceral Athan viz., Kalamkay-k-kanni Nar Muti-c-ceral, Katal Pirakkottiya Cenkuttuvan and Atukot-Pattu-c-ceral Athan. The rest of the book relate to the Irumporai family; the VII Ten belongs to Selvakkatunko Vazhi Athan, the VIII Ten to Perum Ceral Irumporai, the conqueror of Thakatur and the IV Ten to Ilam Ceral Irumporai, the son, the grandson and the great grandson respecvitvely of Antuvan Ceral.
Various places of importance, the great chiefs and chieftains, the foreigners like Yavanas, the warfare and important battlefields, the fivefold classification of the country and other geographical details are all alluded to in this anthology. The poets of this anthology and the literary patronage of the Ceras are not myths. Paranan Kannam Kannan Katu, Vezhakkadu (Umbarkadu) and Kakkaiyur, still existing in Malayalam country, bear testimony to the conferment of Jaghirs on the Poets Paranar, Kumattur Kannanar and Kakkai-p-Padiniyar by the Cera kings, Cenkuttuvan, Imayavaramban Netun Ceral Athan, and Atukotpattu-c-Ceral Athan respectively.
This book is important as revealing the culture, the custom and practice, the political and military life of the Tamil land; of the first few centuries of the Christian era. It is interesting to note that the conception of the fundamental unity of India, from Himalayas to Cape Comorin, goes back, to the poems of the sangam Age ( verse 1 and 43 of this anthology). Politics had become, by that time, an all India Science and the Yagas, varying according to the gradation of sovereignty, were believed to have a magical influence in establishing an ever expanding empire.  This inspired the ambitious kings of Tamil land to perform the Royal sacrifices; and the study of their sacred texts and related literature became very popular. Further, the political unrest in the North drove the Sanskrit, Pali and Prakrit scholars to South India. Manimekalai, the Tamil epic reveals the Taml land as a centre of all-India learning, with its intellectual capital at Kanchipuram. The beginning of this development is seen in Patirruppattu itself.
The Yagas are mentioned in many places. The Rajasuya was not unknown; there was a Cola of the name Rajasuyam Vetta Peru Nar Killi i.e. Nal Killi the Great who had performed the Rajasuya Yaga. There was the great Pandya of many yagas viz. Palyakacalai Muthu Kutumi-p-Peru Vazhuthi. The Ceras, as seen from this book, were no exceptions. The Putra Kameshti yaga is, it may be suggested, mentioned in poem No.74 by Arisilkizhar, a Non-Brahmin poet. There we learn that the queen donned on her beautiful shoulders a circular skin of the stag, well cut out and decked with pearls and precious stones.Was the skin made thus into a valuable amulet? In the Atharva Veda are two charms for obtaining a son ( III 23 & VI.11). The second of these mantras is relevant to the study of this Putra-kameshti. This consists of three parts and when the third part, which runs thus “May Prajapati elsewhere afford the birth of a female but here shall bestow a man” was recited, according to the sutras (Kans 35-9) which explain the procedure, “The fire is surrounded with the wool of a male animal and the wool is tied upon the woman” (probably as an amulet). Instead of the wool we find the skin of the stag, the male animal, being used in the sacrifice performed by the Cera king.
This reference to this Putra-kameshti is very important. The question is very often raised whether the Cera who ruled over a country where the MarumakkalTayam or matriarchal succession now reigns supreme, were following the law of Makkal Tayam or patriarchal succession, as their colleagues the Colas and the Pandyas did or were following the law of Marumakkal Tayam, as followed of the kings of Malayalam today. The wife of the king under the Marumakkal Tayam is never called the Queen. InPattirruppattu, every cera king is praised as the husband of the chaste consort. But his does not help us to decide the issue raised. The Putra-kameshti poem, however, conclusively proves, it was the son of the consort that becomes the king, thus establishing beyond doubt the patriarchal succession of these kings. There is one other difficulty, for the Padikam speaks of the mothers of these kings as “ Velavikoman Pathuman Devi” etc.  It is this kind of expression that has really created the confusion. Devi ordinarily means a wife, this phrase will then denote a wife of  a Velir chief Pathuman etc. How can the wife of a chief be also wife of the Cera King? This leads some scholars to assume that the succession was matriarchal where the mother of the ruling prince is never the wife of a king. But as this theory runs counter to the explicit statement of the Putra kameshti poem. One has to explain the word according to Thiru T.V.Sadasiva Pandarathar as meaning “daughter,” a usage made clear by such phrases as Cera ma Devi, Pancavan ma Devi, all wives of Colas and not of Ceras or Pandyas. Or Ceran ma devi etc. may be an elliptical shorthand expression for “The great Cola queen, the daughter of the Pandya or Cera.” Names like Sentan korran or Kiran Korran etc. mean Korran son of Centan or Kiran. Therefore Patuman Ma Devi mean the Queen, the daughter of Pathuman. One is justified in referring to the usage of the Imperial Cola Inscriptions in view of the close kinship that exists between the Meykkirtis of the later Colas and the Patikams of Patirruppattu as explained by Tiru T.V.Sadasiva Pandarathar in his short introduction to the present commentary.
In other places also, the Cera kings are praised in Patirruppattu for bringing forth children. The theory of three debts or duties to the Devas, the ancestors, and the learned, to be discharged respectively, by every man, by performing sacrifices, by bringing forth children, and by learning the ancient texts, it, as seen by this very poem and poem No. 70 as old as the Sangam age. Therefore, when Parimelazhagar speaks of this in his commentary on the chapter on Children in Tirukkutal, he is not going against any Tamil tradition.
There is an old commentary on Patirruppattu, whose importance cannot be easily exaggerated; but to the modern reader it is but a series of algebracial formula. The present commentary explains all that is necessary for elucidating the text for the man in the street - the defied abstraction of modern democracy; and serves, therefore, at a valuable key for unlocking the closely preserved treasure - chest of the old commentary.
The Sangam poets caught the spirit of the poetic moment and enshrined it in the most appropriate and correct poetic phrase, afraid of spoiling its effect by any elaboration. Brevity is the life of their poetry. This explains why the anthologies of the Sangam verses are arranged according to the length of verses as Kurum Togai, Nedun Togai, Aim Kuru Nuru etc. In every poem there is heart or life centre - a beautiful phrase which is the very quint - essence of the poem and this phrase by common acceptance and appreciation, becomes according to Sangam usage the very name of the verse. This is seen in every one of the verses in the present work. The new commentary has brought out the poetic significance of all these poetic phrases, thus helping us to understand the poetic theory of the Sangam age.
On an occasion like this, one cannot but think with reverential gratitude, of the late lamented Dr. Swaminatha Aiyar, but for whose untiring zeal and toil we could not be boasting either of Patirruppattu or its ancient commentary. What has been thus made available is now made more and more popular by the present commentator.  My friend Tiru Vellaivaranan has brought out the importance of the new commentary. Whether one agrees with all the points or not one has to agree that this commentary is very valuable for a close study of the ancient work by the modern man. I deem it, therefore, a great privilege, as desired by my friend Thiru Avvai Duraiswami Pillai, to introduce, with heartfelt thanks, this work, to the ever grateful public of Tamil land.
Madras
26.10.49								T.P.Meenakshisundaran


muṉṉurai
	kaṟṟataṉā lāya payaṉeṉkol vālaṟivaṉ 
	naṟṟāḷ toḻāar eṉiṉ.
caṅkat tokainūlkaḷ eṭṭuttokaiyum pattup pāṭṭumeṉa vakaiyāl  iraṇṭākiyum, viriyāl patiṉeṭṭā kiyum nilavuvaṉavākum. ivaṟṟuḷ patiṟṟuppatteṉpatu eṭṭuttokaiyuḷ oṉṟākum. itu pappattāka amainta pattukkaḷ pattuk koṇṭateṉṟum, nūṟu pāṭṭukkaḷ koṇṭateṉṟum patiṟṟuppattu eṉappaṭum peyarālē aṟiyalām. itaṉ ovvoru pattum ovvoru cēra vēn taṉaip paṟṟi vēṟu vēṟu āciriyaṉmārāl pāṭappaṭṭuḷatu. inta āciriyaṉmārkaḷum cēravēntarkaḷum oru kālattavarākavum vēṟu vēṟu kālattavarākavum karutappaṭu kiṉṟaṉar. patiṟṟuppat teṉṉum peyar ippāṭṭukkaḷaip pappattāka eṭuttut tokuttōrāl iṭappeṟṟa peyarātal vēṇṭum.
eṭṭut tokaiyuḷ kāṇappaṭum naṟṟiṇai, kuṟuntokai, aiṅkuṟunūṟu, patiṟṟuppattu, paripāṭal, kalittokai, akanāṉūṟu, puṟanāṉūṟu eṉṟa eṭṭaṉuḷ, puṟapporuḷ vakaiyil amaintavai patiṟṟuppattum, puṟanāṉūṟum eṉṟa iraṇṭumākum. ivaiyiraṇṭum, ēṉaiyavaṟṟuḷ naṟṟiṇai, kalittokai yeṉṟa iraṇṭu moḻinta piṟa yāvum kālañ ceṉṟa perumpulavar ṭākṭar tiru. u. vē. cāminātaiyaravarkaḷāl pala āṇṭukaṭku muṉpē pala ēṭukaḷiṉ tuṇai koṇṭu ārāyntu cevviya muṟaiyil veḷiyiṭappeṟṟuḷḷaṉa. avaṟṟuḷ patiṟṟuppattu 1904-ām āṇṭil mutaṉmutalāka acciṭappeṟṟu veḷiyāyiṟṟu. ivvāṟē tamiḻakattut tamiḻaratu ilakkiyap paḻañcelvamāy, pala nūṟṟāṇṭukaṭku muṉ vāḻnta tamiḻ naṉmakkaḷuṭaiya nākarikap paṇpāṭukaḷai yuṇarttum nalviḷakkamāyt tikaḻum intat tokai nūlkaḷaic cemmaiyuṟa ārāyntu iṉṟum eṉṟum tamiḻ payilvōr aṉaivarum orumukamākap pārāṭṭip paravattakka vakaiyil veḷiyiṭuvatākiya ariya tamiḻppaṇi purinta ṭākṭar tiru. aiyaravarkaṭkut tamiḻulaku peritum kaṭamaippaṭṭuḷatu.
tiru. aiyaravarkaḷ mutaṉmutalāka veḷiyiṭṭapōtē itaṟkup paṇṭaic cāṉṟōr oruvar eḻutiya uraiyum avarkku uṭaṉ kiṭaittamaiyiṉ, mutal veḷiyīṭṭilē patiṟṟuppattu mūlamum paḻaiya vuraiyum eṉa veḷiyiṭṭu, itaṉai aṟiñar kaṇṭu poruḷaṟintu iṉpuṟum vāyilaiyum utaviyatu peritum pōṟṟattakkatākum. “ivvurai illai yāyiṉ, innūṟ poruḷai ikkālattil aṟintukoḷḷutal mika aritu” eṉa avarkaḷē uraittiruppatu kāṇka. ēṭukaḷil uraikārar peyar kuṟikkappaṭāmaiyiṉ avar iṉṉāreṉṟu aṟivatu iyalātāyiṟṟu. āyiṉum, avar nēminātam ceyta kuṇavīra paṇṭitar kālattukkup piṟpaṭṭavareṉpatu orutalai. patiṟṟuppattiṉ uraiyil,cillērāḷareṉṟaviṭattuc “ciṉmaiyaic ciṉṉūl eṉṟatupōla īṇṭuc ciṟumaiyākak koḷka” (patiṟ.76:1) eṉṟaviṭattu, uraikārarāl ciṉṉūl eṉappaṭuvatu kuṇavīra paṇṭitar eḻutiya nēmināta meṉṉum nūlukkup peyar.
ivvaṇṇam pāṭṭum uraiyumākak kiṭaikkum ippatiṟṟup
pattu, mutaṟ pattum pattām pattum iṉṟi iṭainiṉṟa eṭṭup pattukkaḷē koṇṭuḷatu. kiṭaikkum ēṭukaḷ palavaṟṟiṉum mutaṟ pattum iṟutip pattum kāṇappaṭavillai. pāṭṭum uraiyum koṇṭa ēṭoṉṟil, oṉpatām pattiṉ iṟutiyil, “patiṟṟuppattu mūlamum uraiyum muṭintatu; cupamastu” eṉṟu kāṇappaṭukiṟatu. mūlamēyuḷḷa ēṭukaḷum oṉpatām pattōṭē muṭikiṉṟaṉa. ivvāṟē toṭakkamum iraṇṭām pattaiyē koṇṭu pala ēṭukaḷum uḷḷaṉa. itaṉāl neṭunāḷkaḷukku muṉpē, itaṉ mutaṟ pattum pattām pattum maṟaintaṉa eṉak koḷḷa vēṇṭiyirukkiṟatu.
iṉi, kiṭaittuḷḷa ovvoru pattukkum patikam oṉṟu kāṇappaṭukiṟatu. atu, pāṭappaṭṭa cēravēntaṉuṭaiya meykkīrttipōl niṉṟu, pāṭiṉōr, pāṭappaṭṭōr, pāṭiya pāṭṭu, pāṭippeṟṟa paricil, pāṭappaṭṭa vēn taṉuṭaiya āṭcik kālam eṉṟa ivaṟṟaik kūṟukiṟatu. appatikaṅkaḷ, tām uṭkoṇṭu niṟkum pāṭṭukkaḷ ovvoṉṟukkum avvap pāṭṭiṉuṭ kāṇappaṭum coṟṟoṭa roṉṟāṟ peyar kuṟittuḷḷaṉa. ovvoru pāṭṭiṉ iṟutiyilum ap pāṭṭiṟkut  tuṟai, vaṇṇam, tūkku, peyar eṉṟa ivai vakukkappeṟṟuḷḷaṉa. ip peyarkaḷē patikattilum tokuttuk kāṭṭappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. mēlum, ip patikaṅkaḷ uraiyuḷḷa ēṭukaḷiṟṟāṉ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. paḻaiyavurai ip patikaṅ kaṭkum urai kuṟittuḷḷatu. āṉāl, ip patikaṅkaḷ uraiyillāta mūlappakutiyēyuḷḷa ēṭukaḷil illai. mūlamēyuḷḷa ēṭukaḷil ovvoru pāṭṭiṉ iṟutiyilum tuṟai, vaṇṇam, tūkku, peyar ākiyaṉa kuṟikkappeṟṟum, ov voru pattiṉ iṟutiyilum pāṭiṉōr peyarum pāṭap paṭṭōr peyarum, “imaya varampaṉ neṭuñ
cēralātaṉaik kumaṭṭūrk kaṇṇaṉār pāṭiṉār pattuppāṭṭu muṟṟum” eṉṟāṟpōlak kuṟikkap peṟṟum uḷḷaṉa. ik kuṟippukkaḷai nōkkumiṭattu, patiṟṟuppattup pāṭṭukkaḷait tokut tōrāl vaṇṇam, tūkku, tuṟai, peyar ākiyaṉa vakukkap peṟṟirukkalāmeṉṟum, avarkkup piṉ vanta cāṉṟōr oruvarāl patikaṅkaḷ pāṭic cērkkap peṟṟirukkalā meṉṟum, karututaṟku iṭamuṇṭākiṟatu. ṭākṭar tiru. aiyaravarkaḷum, “ovvoru ceyyuḷiṉ piṉṉum amaintuḷḷa tuṟai, vaṇṇam, tūkku, peyareṉpavaikaḷ uraiyillāta mūlap piratikaḷilellām iruttaliṉ, avai uraiyāciriyarāl eḻutappaṭṭaṉa valla
veṉṟum, nūlāciriyarkaḷālō tokut tōrālō eḻutappaṭṭaṉaveṉṟum; patikaṅkaḷ uraip piratikaḷil maṭṭum kāṇappaṭukiṉṟamaiyāl avaṟṟai iyaṟṟiṉōr  nūlāciriyarallareṉṟum terikiṉṟaṉa. āciriyar nacciṉārkkiṉi yarālum aṭiyārkku nallārālum; tattam uraikaḷil eṭuttāḷap peṟṟiruttaliṉ; ippatikaṅkaḷ avarkaḷ kālattiṟku muntiyavaiyeṉṟu tōṟṟu kiṉṟatu” eṉṟu kūṟuvatu nōkkattakkatu.
cumār patiṉaintu āṇṭukaṭkumuṉ ceṉṉaip palkalaik kaḻaka vittuvāṉ tērvukkuc celvōr cilarukku ip patiṟṟuppattiṉaik kaṟpikkavēṇṭiya kaṭamai eṉakku uṇṭāyiṟṟu. akkālattē avarkaṭku itaṉaik kaṟpittu varukaiyil, itaṟkoru virivurai yiruppiṉ nalamākumeṉum eṇṇamuṇṭāka; eṉ naṇpar cilar vāyilākap patiṟṟup pattiṉ ēṭukaḷ iraṇṭu peṟṟu, accuppaṭiyaiyum avaṟṟaiyum oppu nōkkuvatu mutaṟkaṇ ceyaṟpālateṉa uṇarntu ceytatil cila pāṭavēṟupāṭukaḷum, cila pāṭaṅkaḷiṟ kāṇappaṭṭa aiyaṅkaṭkut teḷivum kiṭaittaṉa. piṉṉar ivvuraip paṇiyai mēṟkoṇṭu ceytuvaruṅkāl, tiruvai yāṟṟu aracar kallūrip pērāciriyarum eṉ vaṇakkat tiṟkuriya āciriyarumākiya karantaik kaviyaracu. tiru.  R. vēṅkaṭācalam piḷḷaiyavarkaḷ tām eḻutivaittirunta urai yiṉaiyum tantu utaviṉārkaḷ. yāṉ eḻuti vaittirunta uraiyai nāvalar tiru. na. mu. vēṅkaṭacāmi nāṭṭāravarkaḷ pārvaiyiṭṭu ippōtu veḷiyāki yirukkum inta muṟaiyaik kāṭṭi ivvakaiyil ivvuraiyai yamaikkumāṟu terivittārkaḷ.
ivvuraiyiṉ amaitiyai nēriṟ kaṇṭu ūkkiyatōṭu viraiya acciṭuvatu nalameṉṟu teruṭṭiya eṅkaḷ arumpeṟal āciriyar tiru. na. mu. vēṅkaṭacāmi nāṭṭāravarkaḷ, itaṉ patikaṅkaḷ ārāyccikku iṭamāka vuḷḷaṉavātalāl, avaṟṟukku urai vēṇṭāveṉap paṇittamaiyiṉ, innūṟ kaṇ patikaṅkaṭku urai yeḻutappaṭavillai. mēlum itaṉ mutaṟ pattu kiṭaik kāmaiyiṉ, itaṟku muṉṉaṇiyil kaṭavuḷ vāḻttuc ceyyuḷ oṉṟu iruntirukku meṉṟum, “eriyeḷḷuvaṉṉa niṟattaṉ” eṉat toṭaṅkuvatum, tol kāppiyap poruḷatikāravuraiyil uraikārarāṟ kāṭṭap paṭuvatumākiya pāṭṭai ip patiṟṟup pattiṉ kaṭavuḷ vāḻttuc ceyyuḷākak kōttu urai yeḻutumāṟum avarkaḷ uraittārkaḷ. urai muḻutum accāki veḷivarum in nāḷil avarkaḷ illāmai eṉ maṉattai varuttukiṟatu.
iṉi, innūliṉ patikaṅkaḷukku urai yeḻutap paṭāmaiyāl, ivaṟṟiṉ karuttu viḷaṅka oru kōvaippaṭutti varalāṟṟu muṟaiyil oru kaṭṭurai yeḻutic cērppatu nalameṉa ivvuraiyaik kaṇṭa aṟiñar kūṟiṉar. iv varalāṟṟut tuṟaiyil yāṉ aṟinta nāṇmutal uḻaittup perumpayaṉ tamiḻulakiṟkaḷittu varupavar eṉ arumpeṟal naṇpar  tiru. T.V. catācivap paṇṭārattāravarkaḷātalāl, avarkaḷai itaṉaic ceyyumāṟu vēṇṭik koṇṭēṉ. avarkaḷum tamakkuḷḷa aluvalkaṭkiṭaiyē uṭal valiyiṉmaiyum poruṭ paṭuttātu patikap pakutipaṟṟiya ciṟanta ārāycci yuraiyiṉai vaḻaṅki yuḷḷaṉar. avarkaṭku eṉ maṉaṅkeḻumiya naṉṟi yuriyatākiṉṟatu.
iṉi, yāṉ eḻutiya uraiyai yāṉē ārāyntu nalan tīṅku kāṇpateṉpatu ciṟitu arumaiyāka iruntamaiyiṉ, urai kaṇṭa eṉṉaip pōlavē pala āṇṭukaḷ vittuvāṉ tērvukkuc celvōrkku itaṉaik kaṟpikkum paṇi mēṟkoṇṭu kūrtta pulamaiyāl ciṟantu niṟkum eṉ ariya naṇpar tiru. ka. veḷḷai vāraṇaravarkaḷai uraipaṟṟiyatoru kaṭṭurai tarumāṟu kēṭṭuk koṇṭēṉ. ataṉai maṟātu ēṟṟu aḻakiya kaṭṭurai tanta avarkaṭkum eṉ maṉamārnta naṉṟi yuriya tākiṉṟatu.
pallavar, cōḻar, pāṇṭiyar eṉṟa iv vēntarkaḷaippaṟṟiya varalāṟukaḷēṉum ōraḷavil makkaḷ aṟintu kōṭaṟ kēṟṟa vakaiyil nūlvaṭivil veḷiyāki irukkiṉṟaṉa. paṇṭai nāḷaic cēra maṉṉarkaḷaippaṟṟiya varalāṟṟiṉaic cevvē aṟintukōṭaṟku vēṇṭum karuvikaḷākac caṅkat tokai nūl kaṭku vēṟāka yātum kiṭaittilatu. iṭaikkālak kalveṭṭukkaḷ paṇṭaic caṅka kālattuc cērar varalāṟṟukkut tuṇai ceyvaṉa vāka illai. cēranāṭṭu moḻiyum naṭaiyum oḻukalāṟum palvēṟu makkaḷ kūṭṭuṟavāl vēṟupaṭ ṭoḻintamai itaṟkuk kāraṇamām; āyiṉum, iṉṟaiya kēraḷa nāṭṭiṉ paṇṭaiya varalāṟṟiṉai ārāyntaṟitaṟku vēṇṭum karuvikaḷum kiṭaittila; kiṭaikkac ceytārumillai. ataṉāl ivvuraikkaṇ teḷivikkappaṭum varalāṟṟuk kuṟippukkaḷ muṭinta muṭipākak kōṭaṟku iṭamillai yeṉpatu teḷivām. vēṟu ārāyccikaḷāl viḷakkamākuṅkāṟum, ivaṟṟai mēṟ kōṭal takkatu. immuyaṟcikkut tuṇaiceyta naṇparum, 1941il vaṭavārkkāṭṭil cillāk kalvit talaivarāka iruntavarumāṉa tiru. irāmaṉ mēṉaṉ avarkaṭku eṉ naṉṟiyuriyatākum.
ivvurai yeḻuti muṭikkappeṟṟatu cila pala āṇṭukaṭku muṉpēyeṉiṉum, iraṇṭāvatu ulakappōr kāraṇamāka, accēṟṟi veḷiyiṭuvateṉpatu ariya ceyalāyiṟṟu. an nerukkaṭi ippōtum tīrntu paṇṭupōl oḻintilatāyiṉum, ittakaiya cīriya centamiḻnūl veḷiyīṭukaḷil caliyātu uḻaittut, tamiḻakattiṟkum, tamiḻmoḻikkum peruntoṇṭu purintu ciṟakkum teṉṉintiya caiva cittānta nūṟpatippuk kaḻakam, ivvuraiyiṉai veḷiyiṭac camaintatu kuṟittup potuvāka ataṟkum, ciṟappāka ataṉaip palavakai uyar paṇikaḷil īṭupaṭutti avvāṟṟāl aḵtu ulavāp perumpukaḻ uṇmait tamiḻnilaiyamākat tikaḻacceytu mēmpaṭum kaḻakac ceyalmuṟait talaivar tiru. va. cuppaiyā piḷḷaiyavar kaṭkum tamiḻakattiṉ cārpil eṉ uḷam niṟainteḻum naṉṟi yiṉait terivittuk koḷḷukiṉṟēṉ.
iṅkē kuṟitta tiruvāḷarkaḷēyaṉṟi vēṟuvakaiyil tuṇaiceyta palarkkum eṉ naṉṟiyaic celuttum kaṭamai yuṭaiyēṉ. palvakaiyilum kuṟaipāṭuṭai yaṉākiya eṉṉai, eṉ arumait tamiḻaṉṉaikkut toṇṭaṉākki āṭ koṇṭaruḷum entai, tillai maṉṟilniṉṟu tiruvaruṭ kūttiyaṟṟum āṭalaracaṉ tiruvaṭip pōtukaḷai maṉa moḻi meykaḷāṟ paravi yamaikiṉṟēṉ.
aṇṇāmalainakar,
31-3-1949								oḷavai. cu. turaicāmi.
